title: Developer Experience Documentation: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Avery Chen
summary: Standards, templates, operating procedures, and canonical support fixes for Developer Experience documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site publishing, and the top support issues we encounter.
body:
Overview

Purpose
This page defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues and their canonical fixes. The goal is to make docs discoverable, reliable, and easy to maintain.

Scope
- All public-facing SDK guides and quickstarts maintained by eng-developer-experience.
- API examples that appear in SDK repos, the docs site, and quickstarts.
- Docs-site publishing and review workflows (CI, review SLOs, and release tagging).
- Canonical list of top support issues with reproducible fixes.

Audience
- Developer Experience engineers and technical writers maintaining docs.
- SDK owners and product engineers who provide examples.
- Support and Solutions teams referencing canonical fixes.

Standards & Authoring Guidelines

1) Writing style and structure
- Use clear, active voice and keep examples minimal but complete.
- Each guide should start with: Intent, Audience, and TL;DR.
- Use headings and short intro paragraphs. Follow with step-by-step instructions and an example section.
- Provide copy-paste-ready code snippets in the primary SDK language and one other (usually Python + JS).

2) Required metadata for every document (top of JSON page)
- title: short, descriptive
- space: eng-developer-experience
- author: real name
- owner_team: engineering|product|customer-success
- status: draft|in_review|published
- created_at and last_updated (YYYY-MM-DD)
- optional: reviewers, labels, related_pages, confidentiality

3) Accessibility and localization
- Use clear headings, alt text for diagrams, and avoid screenshots for procedural steps.
- Flag high-value pages for translation: add label "i18n-candidate" and open a translation request issue.

Document Types & Templates

A. SDK Guide (canonical template)
- Title (concise)
- Intro: intent, audience, prerequisites
- Quickstart (copy-paste example)
- Concepts & API reference pointers
- Advanced usage (config, performance knobs, error handling)
- Troubleshooting & common errors
- Ownership and maintenance notes

B. Quickstart (1-2 page runnable example)
- Goal: 5-10 minute end-to-end demo for a single use-case (e.g., text generation, embeddings).
- Files: README.md, minimal app example (app.py / app.js), requirements.txt / package.json, .env.example
- Steps: Setup, Run locally, Test key flows, Expected outputs

C. API Example (canonical examples)
- Small focused snippets (<= 15 lines) showing the recommended invocation patterns: auth, request, streaming, error handling.
- Languages: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go (where maintained).
- Each example must include comments explaining critical options (timeout, max_tokens, model selection).

D. Template filenames and where to store
- SDK guides: eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/<slug>-YYYY.json
- Quickstarts: eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/<slug>-YYYY.json + repo under github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/<slug>
- API examples: eng-developer-experience/api-examples/<slug>-YYYY.json

Example SDK Guide TOC (recommended)
1. TL;DR
2. Prerequisites
3. Quickstart (Python + JS)
4. Core Concepts
5. API Reference links
6. Advanced configuration (examples and performance notes)
7. Troubleshooting
8. Changelog & Ownership

Quickstarts & Templates: Canonical Checklist
- Clear goal statement (1-2 sentences)
- Minimal prerequisites + automated setup (script or Dockerfile)
- CI test that runs the quickstart smoke test (ideally in < 5 minutes)
- LICENSE: MIT or Apache-2.0 where appropriate
- README with expected output and validation steps

API Examples: Best Practices
- Prefer short, explicit examples over long indented docs.
- Always show authentication example with environment variables:

  ```bash
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED
  ```

- Example Python snippet (canonical pattern):

  ```python
  from redwood import RedwoodClient

  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  resp = client.generate(model="gpt-rw-1", prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello'", max_tokens=32)
  print(resp.text)
  ```

- Example JS snippet (canonical pattern):

  ```javascript
  import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-rw-1', prompt: "Summarize the doc" });
  console.log(resp.text);
  ```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (Publishing Workflow)

Ownership
- DOC_OWNER label required on PR and in the page metadata. Primary owners: eng-developer-experience docs team. Secondary owners: SDK maintainers.

Pull Request workflow
1. Author creates a branch: docs/<short-desc> and updates JSON page or markdown source.
2. Add metadata and front-matter, run local lint: `make docs-lint`
3. CI checks: spellcheck, markdown/json schema validation, broken-link check, sample-code test (runs smoke tests in container).
4. Assign reviewers: must include one engineering reviewer and one product reviewer for public-facing API changes.
5. Merge on green CI and approved review.
6. Publishing: merged changes are auto-deployed to staging and published to production on the next release window (daily 02:00 UTC deploys).

Review SLOs and update cadence
- Critical pages (quickstarts, SDK guides): reviewer response <= 72 hours.
- Minor edits/typo fixes: <= 7 days.
- Ownership review: every 6 months the owner must verify the guide works with supported SDK versions.

Doc CI checks (must pass)
- JSON/YAML schema validation for Confluence export format.
- Link-check (fail on 5xx/4xx except internal draft links).
- Code snippet linting: run language-specific linters where feasible.
- Example smoke test: start container, run quickstart script, validate expected output (exit 0).

Communication & Release Notes
- For breaking changes to SDKs or APIs referenced by docs, create a docs change log entry under product-docs/release-notes and notify #devex-docs slack channel.

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (current list)

Note: This is a living list. When a new top issue is identified, add it here and create a reproducible example in the examples repo.

| ID | Symptom | Likely root cause | Canonical fix | Owner |
|----|---------|-------------------|---------------|-------|
| S-001 | SDK auth errors (401) when using env var | Missing or malformed REDWOOD_API_KEY; token expired | Verify env var name; rotate key; run `redwood auth test` to validate. Add error handling to snippet. | eng-developer-experience |
| S-002 | Streaming hangs / partial responses | Incompatible HTTP client or missing `stream=true` flag | Use recommended client with chunked transfer support; show example for Node fetch and Python requests. | eng-developer-experience |
| S-003 | High latency for short requests | Incorrect batching config or long `max_wait_ms` | Recommend per-route config: max_batch_tokens=64, max_wait_ms=20; provide example rollout. | eng-platform |
| S-004 | Mismatched model names between docs and runtime | Docs referencing deprecated model alias | Update docs to canonical model id (e.g., gpt-rw-1) and add alias table in page. | eng-serving-runtime |
| S-005 | Embedding dimensionality mismatch | Using older embeddings model or wrong vector size | Confirm model in quickstart; run small check script to assert vector length. | applied-ml-and-evals |

Canonical fix example (S-001)
1. Reproduce: run the following in a fresh shell: `unset REDWOOD_API_KEY && python examples/auth_test.py`
2. Inspect the error: `HTTP 401: missing api key`
3. Fix: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<paste-key>"` then re-run.
4. Mitigation: Add explicit check in SDK init and raise helpful error: `ValueError("REDWOOD_API_KEY not set; see docs: /.../auth")`

Oncall & Escalation for Docs-Blocking Issues
- If a docs change is required to mitigate an active incident (oncall detects customer-facing problems), tag @devex-oncall and open emergency docs PR with `EMERGENCY_DOCS` label.
- Emergency PRs are triaged and can be merged by the Docs Team lead after one engineering + one product thumbs-up.

Maintenance & Review Cadence
- Quarterly doc audit: owners must verify smoke tests and update if SDK or API changed.
- Monthly top-issues review during DevEx team retro. Add unresolved items to the backlog.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets
- Local lint run: `make docs-lint`
- Run quickstart smoke test: `docker-compose -f quickstart/docker-compose.yaml run --rm quickstart-test`
- Check JSON schema: `python tools/validate_confluence_json.py path/to/doc.json`
- Create translation request: open issue in repo `devex/translations` with label `i18n-request` and include page id.

Related resources
- Quickstarts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts
- SDK repos: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js
- Docs site ops playbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-site-operating-procedures-2026

Contact & Ownership
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience docs team (docs@redwood-inference.internal)
- Secondary/triage: support@redwood-inference.internal
